mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which is associated with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by ≥ 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly above the 30-day moving average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) suggests improving supply-demand balance, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥ 2% month-over-month while CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain negative despite the trigger (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) followed by a rebound above the prior quarter's level predicts a temporary supply shock that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥ 10% in a quarter then rises by ≥ 5% in the following quarter
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 20-day window following the rebound (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2% in a contractionary direction while the Federal Funds Rate remains unchanged for three months, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days are predicted to be negative due to persistent inflationary pressure.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥ 2% over 12 months and FEDFUNDS remains flat for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 20-day average during the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 3.5% without a corresponding increase in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a tight labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days due to overvalued equities.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% while PAYEMS increases by less than 1% over the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the 30-day moving average during the trigger (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive month of declining retail sales proxies (not available in the catalog; fallback: HOUST for industrial demand) and rising consumer confidence (not available; fallback: UNRATE as proxy for sentiment) predict negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days due to risk-off sentiment.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by ≥ 3% in a month while UNRATE increases by ≥ 0.1 percentage points
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 5-day average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months in a low-rate environment is associated with a higher probability of a soft landing, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for three consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 4.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the trigger window (p > 0.05).
